Reference / io/stream

io/stream#

The roles every byte and text stream of std plays: Reading and Writing for bytes, AsyncReading and AsyncWriting for streams that wait, ReadingText and WritingText for text, ByteSource for something that has bytes, and Closing.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

writer.write(packet);
writer <- "header: " <- payload <- "\n";
writer.flush();
let piece = reader.bytes(4096);          // [] is the end

Description#

The roles every byte and text stream of std plays: Reading and Writing for bytes, AsyncReading and AsyncWriting for streams that wait, ReadingText and WritingText for text, ByteSource for something that has bytes, and Closing.

<- writes any ByteSource; only inside that operator a string is written as strict UTF-8 and an @byte as it is. Explicit writer <- parts... writes each element of the array in order. The operator calls Writing.write and gives back the same Writing, so chains read left to right; a failed write stops the chain.

Writing.write takes the whole source or throws IncompleteWrite.after(written) with the number of bytes taken; it neither retries, nor flushes, nor closes. Reading.bytes(limit) needs limit > 0 and returns at most limit bytes; an empty result is the end, and stays the end.

role AsyncReading#

role AsyncReading

Nominal asynchronous byte input. A positive limit bounds each result; short reads are valid and empty bytes mean permanent orderly EOF. Implementations reject non-positive limits with InvalidReadLimit. Each call returns a lazy Future; repeated await of that Future observes the same read outcome. This role does not imply synchronous Reading, resource ownership or close().

AsyncReading.bytes#

async bytes(limit is int) is @byte

At most limit bytes once they come; [] at the end.

role AsyncWriting#

role AsyncWriting

Nominal asynchronous all-or-failure output, returning the same capability. ByteSource materialization belongs to the started write; failures propagate. A failed write may already have emitted a prefix: no rollback/replay promise. Await each write explicitly; this role has no flush() or synchronous Writing conformance and is not an operand for the synchronous stream-write operator. Concrete socket halves must separately implement serialization and cleanup.

Writes all the bytes of source and gives back this output, for chaining.

Writes all the bytes and gives back this output, for chaining.

Errors#

  • IncompleteWrite.after(written): a write took only the first written bytes.
  • InvalidReadLimit.limit(value): a read limit below one.
